takes the float `xmm1` and picks 3.141593 (`01CEBC50`) when it is at least 0.0, else -3.141593 (`00915620`); only when byte `+3` of `rcx` AND `0xE0` equals `0x60` it adds that offset, subtracts the truncated-to-integer quotient by 6.283185 (`01CEBC78`) times 6.283185, subtracts the offset again and stores the float at `+0xB0` of the object at qword `+0xB8` of `rcx`; otherwise it returns without a store
calls `00263C20(003588B0())` and returns 0 unless it returns 3; when it is 3, returns 1 if `003229A0(ecx)` returns 0, else 0

calls `0031B770(rcx)` and returns 0 when it is null; returns 1 when bit 14 of the result's dword `+0` is set; otherwise returns 1 when its qword `+0x708` is non-zero and its word `+0x714` is at most `0x21E` (unsigned), else 0
calls `00267E10(r9)` and `00269FE0(rdx, that result)`, then tail-jumps `00263A30(byte +0x15 of rdx, word +0 of rdx)`

notes: No doubts. 0026AA60 computes the offset add before the byte +3 guard, but only the guarded path stores; the 0.0 compare is a comiss against xorps zero, so a NaN xmm1 takes the -3.141593 arm. 003528C0's tail-call argument order is rcx = byte +0x15, edx = word +0 of the original rdx (rbx).
